 Court No. - 29 
 Hon'Ble Manoj Bajaj, J. 
Applicant-Rukmani Singh (informant) has filed this application under Section 482 Code of Criminal
Procedure for setting aside the order dated 30.07.2025 passed in Case No.763 of 2024, titled State
Vs. Sukhmeena Singh and others, by the court of Additional Civil Judge (Senior Division)/IInd
Acjm, Ayodhya, whereby the application by complainant seeking further investigation has been
rejected.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that on the basis of the complaint by applicant/informant the prosecution of four accused persons, namely, Sukhmina Singh, Shyam Lal Singh, Girish Singh and Devesh Singh (opposite party nos.3 to 6) started with registration of Case Crime No.291 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. wherein the charge-sheet against the accused persons under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. stands filed.

He submits that the opposite party no.1 is the sister of the applicant, who had filed Civil Suit no.126 of 2011 before the Civil Court, Faizabad,
wherein four advocates, namely, Ram Milan Shukla, Amit Shukla, Girijesh and R.N.Shukla allegedly represented the applicant, but the said advocates were never engaged by the applicant.

According to the learned counsel someone impersonating as Rukmani Singh engaged those counsels to help the plaintiff/opposite party no.3, therefore, the accused persons are being prosecuted for the alleged offence of cheating and fraud.

Learned counsel has argued that though the investigation in the case is complete as the charge-sheet has been filed but the statements of the four advocates, who had filed joint power of attorney on behalf of the applicant in the civil suit were not recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Therefore, an application was moved before the trial court for conducting further investigation, but the same has been dismissed vide impugned order dated 30.07.2025.
He prays that the impugned order be set-aside and further investigation be ordered.

During the course of hearing, it is fairly stated by learned counsel that after acquiring the knowledge of the alleged fraud committed before the civil court by the opposite party no.3 with the help of other accused persons, no application was moved by the applicant to apprise the civil court about the conduct of the plaintiff or anyone else.

After hearing learned counsel for the applicant and considering the submissions, this Court does not find any merit in the application as the ground that the four advocates were not authorized to represent the complainant before the civil court has not been questioned in any manner, much less by moving any application before the civil court to apprise the misconduct of the plaintiff.

Further a perusal of the impugned order would show that the cognizance of the offence was taken by the Magistrate on 26.07.2024, however, the further proceedings before the trial court had been stayed by this Court vide order dated 20.09.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Application under Section 482 bearing No.8473 of 2024.

The trial court has given valid reasons while dismissing the application filed by the applicant, therefore, finding no merit in the application, this Court not inclined to exercise inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
Resultantly, without meaning any expression of opinion on the merits of the case, the application fails and is hereby dismissed.
